reason: Internal only, and inert unless `[culture] enabled` is turned on. When it is, it changes what Nora reads on ONE occasion: the participation turn, where she decides whether to speak into a room nobody addressed her in. That prompt now carries the room's own account of what it is and why it became that way, written by the daily background fold. It is the only part of that prompt about the room itself rather than about a moment in it — its neighbours answer what was said, what is unsettled and where she had got to; this one answers what this place is like. The account states its own age, because nothing in this tier expires and one written weeks ago can still be right. Everything else deliberately does not read it: the ordinary reply path, the filter that decides whether a message is worth waking for, the background pass that decides whether to raise something unprompted, and the pass that proposes notes. That exclusion is measured, not stylistic — the filter was measured getting worse when given more context. Until this landed, the part that renders this account had no caller anywhere in the codebase, so the tier wrote a fresh account of every room every day and nothing ever read one. The measurement that justified this shipped earlier with the rebuilt evaluation suite, which reconstructs a room's real account at a real past moment rather than reading a written-out one; this change is the wiring that measurement was about. Nothing a member of a room can observe until the tier is enabled.
